glosses: etwas (Akkusativ) haben müssen, um ein bestimmtes Ziel erreichen zu können

examples.text: Ich benötige unbedingt einen neuen Plattenspieler.

glosses: Zeit oder auch andere Ressourcen in Anspruch nehmen

examples.text: Ich benötige noch fünf Minuten!
Zwei Tage, das ist ungefähr die Zeit, die es benötigt, bis das Material durchgetrocknet ist.
Der Hund benötigte all seine Kraft, um wieder aus dem Schlammloch herauszukommen.

glosses: etwas unbedingt verlangen, etwas notwendig machen

examples.text: Der Betrieb einer Dampfmaschine erforderte eine ständige Verfügbarkeit günstiger Brennstoffe, wie Holz oder Kohle.

„Das Motorfliegen erfordert ein beträchtliches navigatorisches Wissen und Können bzw. beim Kunstfliegen vestibuläre Belastbarkeit, Raumorientierungsvermögen und ein feinmotorisches Gespür für den Umgang mit der Maschine.“

glosses: To demand, to insist upon (having); to call for authoritatively.

examples.text: "I am Miss Newbury," I announced, "and I require to be shown to my room immediately, if you please."

‘Regrettably, I have concluded, after considering the matter over Christmas[…], that I can no longer maintain the high standard of service I require of myself, meet the demands of office and cope with the pressures of public life, without my health deteriorating further.’

glosses: Naturally to demand (something) as indispensable; to need, to call for as necessary.

examples.text: Chronic pain is occasionally a sign of a very serious problem, like brain tumors, and can require surgery.
A weapon small enough to put on a missile would require uranium enriched to more than 90% U-235.

glosses: To demand (of someone) to do something.

examples.text: It is required (of me) that I give evidence in court.
After Aug 3 all salesgirls will be required to wear only one style of skirt while on duty: the midi.
The government would like to require non-British fiances who wish to marry a British citizen to sit an English test.

glosses: To ask (someone) for something; to request.

examples.text: I requyre yow lete vs be sworne to gyders that neuer none of vs shalle after this day haue adoo with other, and there with alle syre Tristram and sire Lamorak sware that neuer none of hem shold fyghte ageynst other nor for wele, nor for woo.
I requyre the in the name of god, that thou torment me nott.

glosses: The desire to purchase goods and services.

examples.text: Prices usually go up when demand exceeds supply.

Nevertheless, it is clear that the global energy demand for air-conditioning will grow substantially as nations become more affluent, with the consequences of climate change potentially accelerating the demand.

glosses: The amount of a good or service that consumers are willing to buy at a particular price.
A forceful claim for something.

examples.text: Modern society is responding to women's demands for equality.

The humor of my proposition appealed more strongly to Miss Trevor than I had looked for, and from that time forward she became her old self again;[…]. Our table in the dining-room became again the abode of scintillating wit and caustic repartee, Farrar bracing up to his old standard, and the demand for seats in the vicinity rose to an animated competition.

glosses: A requirement.

examples.text: His job makes many demands on his time.
There is a demand for voluntary health workers in the poorer parts of Africa and Asia.

glosses: An urgent request.

examples.text: She couldn't ignore the newborn baby's demands for attention.

glosses: An order.
More precisely peak demand or peak load, a measure of the maximum power load of a utility's customer over a short period of time; the power load integrated over a specified time interval.
To request forcefully.

examples.text: I demand to see the manager.

glosses: To claim a right to something.

examples.text: The bank is demanding the mortgage payment.

According to this saga of intellectual-property misanthropy, these creatures [patent trolls] roam the business world, buying up patents and then using them to demand extravagant payouts from companies they accuse of infringing them. Often, their victims pay up rather than face the costs of a legal battle.

glosses: To ask forcefully for information.

examples.text: I demand an immediate explanation.

When Lazarus left his charnel-cave,
⁠And home to Mary’s house return’d,
⁠Was this demanded—if he yearn’d
To hear her weeping by his grave?

glosses: To require of someone.

examples.text: This job demands a lot of patience.

glosses: To issue a summons to court.

glosses: Dire ou prier de donner, d’apporter, d’expédier quelque chose, d’envoyer ou d’aller chercher quelqu’un, etc.

examples.text: Ôtez donc vos boutons en diamant, qui valent chacun cent mille francs ; cette singesse vous les demanderait ; et, pour les offrir à une fille, autant les mettre à mes oreilles.

glosses: Demander en mariage.

examples.text: Je suis venu vous demander votre fille.

glosses: Faire savoir que l'on cherche quelque chose ou quelqu'un.

examples.text: Il y a deux catégories de chercheurs qui ne cherchent plus. Ceux qui ont trouvé, en général multirécompensés, qui passent leur temps à intervenir dans des émissions télévisées et finissent conseillers du gouvernement. Et ceux qu’on a licenciés, nettement moins demandés.

glosses: Chercher quelqu’un pour le voir.

examples.text: On est venu pour vous demander. - Qui demandez-vous ? - On vous demande.

glosses: Chercher à savoir, à connaître en questionnant.

examples.text: Que voulez-vous, Monsieur ? demanda-t-elle au jeune homme d’une voix qui bruit à ses oreilles comme une musique délicieuse.
